fact: Kayode Adeniyi says a consultancy team on the Central Bank of Nigeria's Anchor Borrowers' Programme in 2021 was using satellite information and GeoAI with farmers.

The Agriculture Ministry signed an MoU with NASRDA under which, the minister said, NASRDA will provide satellite imagery and real-time monitoring for a national framework on produce traceability and farmland monitoring.
system: National Framework for Agricultural Produce Traceability and Farmland Monitoring

fact: UNCTAD says Nigeria, with NASRDA as lead partner, has used the CropWatch cloud system since 2021 for crop condition, acreage and yield assessments and pest and drought early warnings.
UNCTAD says CropWatch work in Nigeria feeds a quarterly bulletin informing government policy, with the January to April 2024 bulletin reporting rainfall 64% below the 15-year norm.

Punch reports that NASRDA launched Crop Watch in Abuja, a satellite-based agricultural monitoring system using remote sensing and ground data to evaluate crop growth and yield, with UNCTAD and the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
NASRDA states that it produces Nigeria CropWatch crop-monitoring bulletins from satellite data with AIRCAS, under a 4 July 2022 MoU, and mails them to federal ministries, departments and agencies.
NASRDA shows bimonthly CropWatch bulletins for October 2025 and February 2026, disseminated to institutions through a mail list.

NASRDA reports the launch in Abuja of an EU-funded, ESA-implemented Earth Observation-based Agricultural Innovations Project with NASRDA, which will use satellite imagery to monitor crops, land cover and predict yields.

Data Science Nigeria says the Gates-funded Edo State Data Governance platform includes an NDVI and geospatial mapping component giving satellite-driven agricultural monitoring and land-use insights to the state Ministry of Agriculture (subnational, Edo State).
system: Edo Data Governance platform (NDVI geospatial component)
